Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as b0f478ea2e516add6a6846edc32eb208a54c15b5
Should we add link to redfish port schema for reference and specify which dbus property maps to which property in schema?
Acknowledged
can we consider making property names same as redfish schemas?
I don't think we do that (in some cases avoid it to make the interface very RF specific).
Doesn't this imply PCIe, which "Port" is not required to be?
Yes, I did have the same thought, so I added that the default value of 0 can indicate not applicable. Do you suggest a better way of indicating applicability (a different interface)?

Thinking more about this, it doesn't have to be just Lanes. Port width is not a concept restricted to PCIe, so changed this to width. There still is a default value where this is unknown, so apps can always check. Resolving, let me know if you're expecting a different solution.
can we consider making property names same as redfish schemas?
Same as above.
Should this be double, since associate redfish property `CurrentSpeedGbps` is also double. - https://redfish.dmtf.org/schemas/v1/Port_v1.xml
Acknowledged
Need a better description here.  What does a speed of "1" represent?  Bits?  Bytes?  PCIe Generation?  PHY speed? Protocol speed?
Doh! Missed this.
This is great!
Acknowledged

Generally we don't put units on these kinds of things.  It's pretty likely we would have a 10mbps port, which wouldn't be able to be represented by this cleanly.

Also, using a float here causes some level of division issues if you want to convert to bits/bytes per second, so we should just avoid those.

Lets just convert this to a uint64, measured in bits per second.  We can treat 0 as the "not available" number.
Acknowledged

We need to differentiate these two.  Lets say

maxint indicates this value is not supported
0 indicates this value is not available at this time.
Acknowledged
And which value conveys that it's not supported on this port?  Not all ports can convey speed.  Need to do the same thing you did for width below.
Acknowledged
nit: Width?
Acknowledged
What does `default: maxint` mean then?  I would think `maxint` is equivalent to "unknown".
Meaning of the default value is noted in the previous line to indicate the property is not supported (in other words unknown), so isn't this what you expect already?
I guess I don't understand the distinction between "not available" and "not supported".  You should probably be clearer on both of them if you intend it to be two different cases.

Yes, I did want to distinguish property not supported by this port vs the value is unknown at a point of time (for eg because the port is inactive). I have noted this in the text. Please let me know if it is clearer now.
Acknowledged
Can I get re-reviews on this?
@patrick@stwcx.xyz could you re-review this?
